quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The best gear to wear when riding is:

options.text: Gear that protects you.
The cheapest gear available.
Gear that looks good.
Any gear that fits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gear that protects you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. The best choice is a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be driving slowly while looking for parking.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars create dangers. A driver might pull out of a parking space into your path without looking. Car doors may open into your lane, and people may step out from between cars.

questions.question: Before riding a motorcycle, you should check everything except:

options.text: Tire air pressure.
Fluid levels.
Turn signals.
Paint damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Paint damage.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals. Paint damage is not a safety concern.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only needed when carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: You don't need to check the tire pressure.
It will handle the same as your own bike.
The owner made sure the brakes work, so you don't have to.
Keep extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself more time to react.
questions.explanation: When borrowing a motorcycle, do the same pre-ride safety checks as you would on your own bike. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar motorcycle and keep extra space for stopping.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You are preventing other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position makes you more visible.

questions.question: When preparing to pass, ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It gives you a better view of the road ahead.
It blocks your view of the road ahead.
It makes it hard to see the vehicle you're passing.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing to see farther ahead and to be more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: Conditions make it harder to stop than normal.
You want to look at the scenery.
You want other drivers to cut you off.
You want the driver ahead to not know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions make it harder to stop than normal.
questions.explanation: Use extra space if your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Increase your distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has a similar effect to:

options.text: Using the brakes.
Speeding up.
Swerving.
Turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear works like braking. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicles' lights better.
Harder than riding during the day because visibility is worse.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because visibility is worse.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well and other drivers cannot see you as well. Without sunlight, it is harder to judge distances.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:

options.text: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
Allow your feet to breathe.
Have tall heels.
Are made of soft, flimsy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them.
Encourage them to ride on quiet roads.
Not get involved.
Take their keys.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have been drinking. Do whatever you can to stop them, including taking their keys. Help arrange a safe way for them to get home.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
In the part of the lane where the car driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where the car driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the car driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This usually means riding in the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Are not as effective as eyeglasses at protecting your eyes.
Do not provide any protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. Only a face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses are not enough protection.

questions.question: To get the best protection, be sure your helmet:

options.text: Meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
Looks sturdy.
Is inexpensive.
Is in your favorite color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: Which material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Wool
Polyester
Silk

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Wear clothing made of leather that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal riding routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided because other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal riding routine.
questions.explanation: You need to know what is behind you for safety. Check your mirrors frequently as part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Lifting off your seat allows your legs to absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Restricts your side vision.
Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
Is usually uncomfortable.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly lowers your chances of serious head or neck injury in a crash. It will not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: At night.
Not during the day.
Never.
Not at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: At night.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing at night to make yourself more visible to other drivers. Bright colors and reflective materials help other people see you on the road.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
Side effects may still remain.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What is a main purpose of wearing a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: It makes you look cool.
It is usually too warm to wear.
It protects you in a crash.
It should not be worn while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding for protection. Leather jackets protect you against injury in a crash and can help protect you in warm weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: Which clothing choice is NOT good for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
Leather gloves.
A baseball cap to cover your hair.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not protect you.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane behind you.
Only the lane next to you.
Most of your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. A properly adjusted mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but your main focus should be on the road behind and beside you.
